In this section, we use data from Environmental Data Initiative (EDI) on Coastal Giant Salamanders collected in HJ Andrews Experimental Forest, Oregon. Measurements were taken in two sections of Mack Creek: one located in old-growth forest (OG) and the other in a clear-cut area (CC) harvested in 1963. The dataset is extracted from the `and_vertebrates` dataset of the `R` package `lterdatasampler`.

Forest harvesting can influence stream conditions, which may affect salamander growth and body size. A scientist is interested in testing whether there is a difference in average weight of Coastal Giant Salamanders between OG and CC. We will use a two-sample t-test to assess whether salamander size differs significantly between the two sites.

::: {style="text-align:center;"}

```{r, results='asis'}

  list(value="\\( H_0: \\mu_{OG} = \\mu_{CC} \\), \\( H_a: \\mu_{OG} < \\mu_{CC} \\)",
       feedback = "No, we want to test if there is a difference, not if one is larger than the other.")
)
# render QA environment
render_q_a_env(opts)
```

### Question 4
One of your colleague run the following test to compare the two locations (OG and CC):
```{python, echo=TRUE}
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats
df_salamander = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ELSTE-Master/Data-Science/main/Data/salamander_weights.csv")

# Variable of interest
weight_CC = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="CC"]
weight_OG = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="OG"]
# Perform independent two-sample t-test (assuming unequal variances)
t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(weight_CC, weight_OG, equal_var=False)

print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.3f}")
print(f"p-value: {p_val:.3f}")
```

He concludes that there is no evidence from the data to suggest that the average weight of Coastal Giant Salamanders differs between the two locations. What do you think  of this procedure?


```{r, results='asis'}
# Define questions choice and individual feedback for each question

opts <- list(
list(
value = "The procedure is appropriate. The t-test is robust to outliers and non-normality.",
feedback = "No, the t-test is sensitive to outliers, which can distort the results."
),
answer = list(
value = "The t-test may not be appropriate because there are outliers.",
feedback = "Yes! The presence of outliers makes the t-test unreliable."
),
list(
value = "The t-test is wrong because it assumes equal variances, which is not the case here.",
feedback = "No, the argument `equal_var = FALSE` already performs Welch’s t-test, which does not assume equal variances."
),
list(
value = "The test should compare the variances instead of the means.",
feedback = "No. The goal is to compare the central tendency (mean or median), not the variability."
)
)
# render QA environment
render_q_a_env(opts)
```

### Question 6
Complete the code below to test whether the average size of Coastal Giant Salamanders differs between the two locations (OG and CC) using the appropriate test you selected in Question 5.


:::: {.panel-tabset}

## Exercise

```{pyodide}
#| exercise: ex_7
import pandas as pd
import scipy.stats as stats

df_salamander = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ELSTE-Master/Data-Science/main/Data/salamander_weights.csv")
df_salamander.head()

# Variable of interest
weight_CC = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="CC"]
weight_OG = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="OG"]

stat, p_value = ______(weight_CC, weight_OG)
print(f"Mann-Whitney U test statistic: {stat}")
print(f"p-value: {p_value}")

```

## Hints

::: { .hint exercise="ex_7"}
Consider using the function `mannwhitneyu()` from `scipy.stats`.

:::

## Solution

::: { .solution exercise="ex_7" }

```python
import pandas as pd
import scipy.stats as stats

df_salamander = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ELSTE-Master/Data-Science/main/Data/salamander_weights.csv")
df_salamander.head()

# Variable of interest
weight_CC = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="CC"]
weight_OG = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="OG"]

stat, p_value = stats.mannwhitneyu(weight_CC, weight_OG)
print(f"Mann-Whitney U test statistic: {stat}")
print(f"P-value: {p_value}")
```

:::

### Question 7
Based on the p-value you obtained, what can you conclude (assuming $\alpha=0.05$)

```{r, results='asis'}
opts <- list(
list(
value = "We accept the null hypothesis that the median sizes are equal between OG and CC.",
feedback = "No. We never accept the null hypothesis. A p-value below \\(0.05\\) leads us to reject it."
),
answer = list(
value = "We reject the null hypothesis and conclude that the median salamander size differs between OG and CC.",
feedback = "Yes! Since the p-value is below \\(0.05\\), we have evidence that the medians differ between the two groups."
),
list(
value = "We conclude that salamanders from OG are heavier than those from CC.",
feedback = "Not necessarily, the test only indicates that a difference exists, not its direction unless the alternative hypothesis was one-sided."
),
list(
value = "We cannot conclude anything because the test only works for normal data.",
feedback = "No, the Mann–Whitney U test is non-parametric and does not require normality."
)
)
# render QA environment
render_q_a_env(opts)
```
